McKane, A. and Hasanbeigi, A. (2010). Motor Systems Efficiency Supply Curves. United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), Vienna, December 2010 (UN-Energy; prepared by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory). No report number or DOI printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 8). Expert-elicited motor-system measures for pumping (10), compressed air (16) and fan (10) systems: % efficiency improvement over LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH base cases, useful life and typical capital cost per system in five motor-system size classes (Tables 7-9), plus supply curves for US, Canada, EU, Thailand, Vietnam and Brazil (Tables 14-51) and country data (Appendix A.1). Main file: MEDIUM base case only (assigned to US, Canada and EU, Table 6): the three system baselines and 12 measures matching machine-drive archetypes. SEC is derived as electricity input per GJ of useful system output = 1/(base efficiency x (1 + improvement)), the source's own method (Sect. 3.4.3), the same framing as the UKERC Motors rows that cite this source (UKERC pump baseline 2.5 GJ/GJ = 1/0.40). Capex: printed US$ per system converted to US$/kW with the source's representative size per class (50/75/150/350/750 hp, p.30) at 0.746 kW/hp, one row per size class with [size] leading the note. _measures: all 36 measures with LOW/MED/HIGH improvements, size-class costs, lifetimes and labour adjustment factors, and 216 country supply-curve rows (individual GWh/yr derived from the printed cumulative values; final CCE in US$/MWh-saved). Not loaded: LOW/HIGH-base SEC for measures (inputs in _measures), supply-curve figures, sensitivity Tables 54-59, maintenance dependence Table 53, labour-cost shares, sector-level appendix rows.

(1) Table 7 prints 1.1.3 twice (1.1.2 in Table 11), and text p.15 numbers impeller trim 1.4.1 while Table 7 has 1.3.1; Table 9 prints 3.1.2 twice and no 3.1.4 (Table 13 has 3.1.2 belt drives, 3.1.3 sediment, 3.1.4 dampers). Codes here follow Tables 11-13. (2) Pump 1.2.1 has "*" in place of a 500-1000 hp cost; fan 3.1.2 belt drives N/A above 200 hp. (3) Vietnam fan cost-effective potential 724 GWh/yr in Table 49 vs 750 in Table 60. (4) Capital costs carry no price year; electricity prices are 2008 US$ (EU 2007). (5) The report uses the full measure cost, not incremental over a standard replacement (p.17), and capital cost only, no O&M change (p.30). (6) System size classes are aggregate motor hp per system; systems over 1000 hp excluded.
